title: Maynard–Tao multidimensional sieve over the (c,d) certificate grid
connection: Maynard–Tao weights (Σλ_{d1..dk})² detect many simultaneous 'prime/structured' events among k linear forms; the ES Type I certificate grid offers many linear-in-(c,d) objects at fixed p (e.g. moduli 4cd, values p²+4c²d).
why: MT weights produce 'at least m of k events happen' from first-moment data only — the shape we want for 'at least one certificate fires' — and here the average is over (c,d) at a single fixed p.
first_step: Write the k-tuple of events E_j = '4c_jd_j·(stuff) has a divisor ≡ −p mod 4c_jd_j' for an admissible family of (c_j,d_j) = (c0+jh, d0) and compute the MT ratio Σ_j S_j / S_0 numerically at p ~ 10^6.
refs: Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Ann. Math. 181 (2015)
BRAINSTORM/technique_transfer_list.md §1

title: Maynard 'dense clusters of primes in subsets' for certificate families
connection: Maynard (Compositio 2016) shows any positive-density subset of admissible linear forms contains many simultaneously prime values; ES certificates are indexed by a dense set of linear forms in the C-parameter (4Cp+1, Cp+...).
why: Gives a combinatorial robustness: we need not control which certificate fires, only that a dense sub-family of forms is admissible at p.
first_step: Check whether the family {4Cp+1 : C ≤ X} with the divisor-in-class event can be recast as primality of auxiliary linear forms f = (4Cp+1)/d for d in a fixed finite set; test admissibility mod small primes.
refs: Maynard, Dense clusters of primes in subsets, Compositio Math. 152 (2016)

title: Zhang / Polymath8 smooth-moduli level of distribution with modulus 4C smooth
connection: Zhang and Polymath8a get primes equidistributed in APs to smooth moduli beyond x^{1/2}; in ES Type I the tied modulus 4C (or 4cd) is free to be chosen smooth.
why: Choosing C among smooth numbers gives well-factorable moduli, which is exactly where beyond-1/2 equidistribution (dispersion + Kloosterman) is available.
first_step: Restrict the ES Type I/II search to C that are y-smooth (y = log^2 p) and measure on data whether R(p) restricted to smooth C keeps the log^2 p main term (p ≤ 10^7).
refs: Zhang, Bounded gaps between primes, Ann. Math. 179 (2014)
Polymath, Variants of the Selberg sieve…, Res. Math. Sci. 1 (2014)

title: Maynard 'Primes in APs to large moduli I–III' with p-dependent residue class
connection: Maynard (2020) extends Bombieri–Vinogradov-type results to moduli up to x^{3/5} for fixed residue classes and (part III) to uniform residue classes; ES needs divisors of p-tied integers in classes −p mod 4C that move with p.
why: Part III's uniformity in the residue class is exactly the feature a p-dependent class needs.
first_step: Read Maynard 'Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli III: uniform residue classes' and write the ES Type II count Σ_e #{ab | (p+e)/4 : a ≡ −b mod e} as a sum over moduli with residue a(p); identify which theorem shape is needed.
refs: Maynard, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli I, arXiv:2006.06572

title: Lichtman beyond-square-root Goldbach/AP methods for tied moduli
connection: Lichtman (2023) improves level of distribution for primes in APs with well-factorable weights to x^{0.617…} and uses it for Goldbach-type counts; ES Type I/II counts are linear-sieve-like sums over moduli 4C.
why: Any improvement in the level for the ES counting function shrinks the exceptional set exponent (repo's E(N) ≪ N exp(−c(log N)^{3/4})).
first_step: Check whether Lichtman's well-factorable weights can be placed on the C-variable (4C | modulus) in the repo's exceptional-set argument (paper/es-threequarter-note.tex).
refs: Lichtman, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli and Goldbach beyond the square-root barrier, arXiv:2309.08522

title: Fouvry–Radziwiłł level of distribution of unbalanced convolutions
connection: Fouvry–Radziwiłł show α*β with one short factor has level of distribution beyond 1/2 for all residue classes; ES divisor counts 1_{ab|N} are convolutions with one short divisor.
why: ES certificates typically use a small divisor a and a large cofactor — the unbalanced regime FR handle.
first_step: Express the Type II e-slice count as Σ_{a small} Σ_{b} 1_{ab = N} with class conditions and check whether FR's theorem (moduli to x^{1/2+δ}) applies when averaging over p in the exceptional-set argument.
refs: Fouvry–Radziwiłł, Level of distribution of unbalanced convolutions, arXiv:1811.08672

title: Guth–Maynard large values of Dirichlet polynomials → short-interval exceptional sets
connection: Guth–Maynard (2024) improve zero-density (Ingham 12/5 → 30/13) via large-values estimates; ES exceptional-set bounds pass through prime counts in short intervals/APs.
why: Zero-density improvements translate to shorter intervals where almost all ES-good primes are detected; could sharpen E(N) or the size of windows where every prime is covered.
first_step: Locate in the repo's exceptional-set notes which zero-density exponent is used and recompute the window exponent with A = 30/13.
refs: Guth–Maynard, New large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, arXiv:2405.20552

title: Matomäki–Radziwiłł at fixed p along the C-progression
connection: MR show bounded multiplicative functions have the same mean in almost all short intervals as in long ones; the integers 4Cp+1 (C varying) form an AP of modulus 4p at fixed p.
why: A short-AP version (Klurman–Mangerel–Teräväinen) could show divisor-class statistics of 4Cp+1 in short C-windows match long averages for one fixed p — pointwise in p, average over C.
first_step: Check whether Klurman–Mangerel–Teräväinen 'multiplicative functions in short arithmetic progressions' covers modulus q = 4p with interval length X = p^{θ}; compute what θ the ES Type I count needs.
refs: Matomäki–Radziwiłł, Multiplicative functions in short intervals, Ann. Math. 183 (2016), arXiv:1501.04585

title: Tao entropy decrement in the C-variable at fixed p
connection: Tao's entropy decrement (log-Chowla two-point, Erdős discrepancy) shows that at most scales the residues of n mod small primes behave independently of the random variable studied; here the random variable is C ↦ 4Cp+1 with p fixed.
why: It converts correlations into averages with a free prime shift — and at fixed p the average over C is legitimate (no averaging over p).
first_step: Formulate: random C ≤ X, X_C = (divisibility pattern of 4Cp+1 by primes ≤ H); compute the empirical mutual information I(X_C ; C mod ℓ) for p = a hard prime from DISPROOF_AVENUES.md.
refs: Tao, The logarithmically averaged Chowla and Elliott conjectures for two-point correlations, arXiv:1509.05422

title: Helfgott–Radziwiłł expansion of divisibility graphs
connection: Helfgott–Radziwiłł (2021) prove expansion of graphs on integers where n ~ n+p if p | n (prime p in a range), improving log-Chowla; ES witnesses are divisibility relations d | N with N in a p-tied family.
why: A divisibility-graph expander on {4Cp+1 : C ≤ X} could transport 'some witness' along edges, the kind of local-to-global step ES lacks.
first_step: Build the graph on C ≤ 10^5 (fixed p) with edges C ~ C' if a common prime ℓ ≤ H divides both 4Cp+1 and 4C'p+1 and compute its spectral gap.
refs: Helfgott–Radziwiłł, Expansion, divisibility and parity, arXiv:2103.06853

title: Pilatte two-point log-Chowla improvement via graph spectra
connection: Pilatte (2023) gets (log X)^{−c} savings for two-point log Chowla using spectral bounds for random-like graphs on integers; same graph-on-divisibility template as Helfgott–Radziwiłł.
why: Quantitative spectral inputs are what a fixed-p C-average argument would need.
first_step: Read Pilatte's graph construction and check whether its vertex set can be replaced by an AP {4Cp+1}.
refs: Pilatte, Improved bounds for the two-point logarithmic Chowla conjecture, arXiv:2310.19357

title: Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao higher uniformity in short intervals
connection: MRT (Annals 2023) prove Gowers/nilsequence uniformity of bounded multiplicative functions in almost all short intervals; ES counts are correlations of multiplicative-type indicator functions along affine forms in C.
why: Uniformity norms control linear-form correlations — e.g. Σ_C 1_{d | 4Cp+1}·1_{class}.
first_step: Write the C-average of the Type I indicator as a correlation of multiplicative functions along linear forms in C and identify which Gowers norm controls it.
refs: Matomäki–Radziwiłł–Tao–Teräväinen–Ziegler, Higher uniformity of bounded multiplicative functions in short intervals on average, arXiv:2007.15644

title: Matthiesen: linear correlations of divisor-type functions
connection: Matthiesen proves asymptotics for correlations of multiplicative functions such as τ, r_2 along systems of linear forms (via Green–Tao nilsequence machinery); ES solution counts at varying (c,d) are such correlations of class-restricted divisor functions.
why: Gives asymptotics with main terms for averaged ES counts over linear families, potentially over thinner families than ET's.
first_step: Check whether 'number of divisors ≡ −1 mod q' restricted divisor functions satisfy Matthiesen's hypotheses (they are not multiplicative but are sums over characters mod q of multiplicative functions).
refs: Matthiesen, Linear correlations of multiplicative functions, arXiv:1606.04482

title: Green–Sawhney 'primes of the form p²+nq²' bilinear technique for p²+4c²d
connection: Green–Sawhney (2024) count primes of the form p² + nq² with p,q prime using Type I/II bilinear sieve on a binary quadratic form; ES Type I concerns divisors of p² + 4c²d, values of the same form shape.
why: Their Type II information on x² + n y² over thin variables is closely aligned with ES's quadratic value p² + 4c²d at fixed p.
first_step: Read Green–Sawhney's Type II estimate and check whether it gives equidistribution of divisors of p² + 4c²d in residue classes mod 4cd when c,d range over boxes at fixed p.
refs: Green–Sawhney, Primes of the form p^2 + nq^2, arXiv:2410.04189

title: Friedlander–Iwaniec asymptotic sieve (x²+y⁴) for thin certificate families
connection: FI breaks parity for primes x²+y⁴ via bilinear forms on a thin quadratic sequence; ES Type I with d a square gives p² + (2cy)², sums of two squares.
why: Restricting to d = y² makes the Type I object a Gaussian norm, where FI-type bilinear technology is designed to work.
first_step: Compute, for p ≤ 10^7, the fraction of primes with an ES Type I certificate having d a perfect square, and whether it stays bounded below.
refs: Friedlander–Iwaniec, The polynomial X^2+Y^4 captures its primes, Ann. Math. 148 (1998)

title: Heath-Brown x³+2y³ cubic parity breaking analogue for norm-form certificates
connection: Heath-Brown's primes of the form x³+2y³ use a Type II estimate on a cubic norm form; ES certificates can be written as divisors of norms from Q(√−d) at fixed p.
why: A norm-form viewpoint replaces 'divisor in residue class' by 'ideal in ray class', where parity-breaking for norm forms exists.
first_step: Write the Type I certificate as: an ideal 𝔞 | (p + 2c√−d) with N𝔞 ≡ −p mod 4cd, i.e. a ray-class condition, and list the ray class field.
refs: Heath-Brown, Primes represented by x^3+2y^3, Acta Math. 186 (2001)

title: Maynard 'primes represented by incomplete norm forms' for ES norm forms
connection: Maynard (Forum Pi 2020) counts primes as norms N(a1ω1+…+akωk) with missing coordinates, using a sieve beyond classical parity; ES Type I divisor event is a norm-divisibility event in quadratic fields.
why: Incomplete-norm-form technology handles thin sets of algebraic integers, relevant to certificates where only a few coordinates vary (c,d at fixed p).
first_step: Check whether 'N𝔞 for 𝔞 | (p+2c√−d)' with c,d in boxes is an incomplete-norm-form set in Maynard's sense.
refs: Maynard, Primes represented by incomplete norm forms, arXiv:1507.05080

title: Maynard primes with restricted digits → thin sets with Fourier control
connection: Maynard (Invent. 2019) counts primes with a missing decimal digit by strong Fourier bounds on the thin digit set; the set of ES-hard residue patterns (Mordell classes mod 840 and deeper digit-like conditions mod 4C) is a digit-like thin set.
why: Template for proving that a thin, Fourier-structured set of p's must intersect the ES-good set.
first_step: Compute the Fourier transform (mod M = 840·k) of the indicator of 'not covered by identities of modulus ≤ M' and compare its L1 norm with Maynard's digit-set bounds.
refs: Maynard, Primes with restricted digits, Invent. Math. 217 (2019), arXiv:1604.01041

title: Merikoski largest prime factor of n²+1 → ES Type I values p²+4c²d
connection: Merikoski (JEMS 2023) shows P⁺(n²+1) > n^{1.279} using Deshouillers–Iwaniec Kloosterman bounds on divisors of n²+1 in ranges; ES Type I needs a divisor of p²+4c²d in a specific class and range.
why: His divisor-in-range distribution for quadratic values is the closest existing tool to 'a divisor of a quadratic value lies in a prescribed window'.
first_step: Re-derive Merikoski's Type I/II information for the polynomial X² + 4c²d (X = p fixed, c varying) and record the admissible divisor ranges.
refs: Merikoski, Largest prime factor of n^2+1, arXiv:1908.08816

title: de la Bretèche–Drappeau level of distribution of quadratic polynomials
connection: de la Bretèche–Drappeau (JEMS 2020) prove level of distribution beyond 1 for #{n ≤ x : q | n² + D} averaged over q; ES Type I is 'f | p² + 4c²d with f ≡ −p (mod 4cd)'.
why: Exactly the object (divisors of a quadratic value) with level > 1 — needed when f is larger than the square root.
first_step: Check whether their result allows a residue condition f ≡ a (mod 4cd) on the modulus f itself, and whether the polynomial variable can be c (with p fixed).
refs: de la Bretèche–Drappeau, Niveau de répartition des polynômes quadratiques et crible majorant pour les entiers friables, JEMS 22 (2020)

title: Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec / Tóth equidistribution of roots of quadratic congruences with modulus condition
connection: Roots ν/f of ν² ≡ −D (mod f) equidistribute (DFI 1995 primes, Tóth composite); ES Type I asks that p be such a root (p² ≡ −4c²d mod f) while f ≡ −p mod 4cd — a joint condition on root and modulus.
why: Joint equidistribution of (root mod f, f mod m) pairs is a natural theorem to aim for and would give averaged Type I counts in new ranges.
first_step: Compute empirically, for D = 4c²d fixed small and f ≤ 10^6, the joint distribution of (ν/f, f mod 4cd) and check for correlation.
refs: Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec, Equidistribution of roots of a quadratic congruence to prime moduli, Ann. Math. 141 (1995)

title: Dunn–Kerr–Shparlinski–Zaharescu bilinear forms with modular square roots
connection: DKSZ bound bilinear sums Σ α_m β_n e(h√(mn)/q) over modular square roots; ES Type I at fixed f involves √(−4c²d) mod f, bilinear in (c, d).
why: Bilinear square-root sums are exactly what appears when one Fourier-expands the Type I condition in c and d.
first_step: Fourier-expand 1_{p² ≡ −4c²d (mod f)} and isolate the bilinear square-root sum; compare with DKSZ hypotheses.
refs: Dunn–Kerr–Shparlinski–Zaharescu, Bilinear forms in Weyl sums for modular square roots and applications, arXiv:1908.10143

title: Kowalski–Michel–Sawin bilinear forms with Kloosterman sums
connection: KMS (Annals 2017) beat Pólya–Vinogradov for bilinear sums of Kloosterman sums in short ranges; ES Type II ff′ = 1 + 4c²dp is a modular hyperbola whose counting leads to Kloosterman sums with modulus tied to (c,d,p).
why: Short-range Kloosterman bilinear bounds are needed precisely because ES moduli 4cd are small relative to the hyperbola size.
first_step: Expand the Type II count for fixed (c,d) into Kloosterman sums S(h, ·; 4cd) and check whether the (c,d)-average is a KMS bilinear form.
refs: Kowalski–Michel–Sawin, Bilinear forms with Kloosterman sums and applications, Ann. Math. 186 (2017), arXiv:1511.01636

title: Bettin–Chandee trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions
connection: Bettin–Chandee bound Σ α_m β_n ν_a e(a·m̄/n); ES exponential sums carry e(h·\overline{4c}/p) or e(h·p̄/4c) fractions with three free variables (h, c, d).
why: Trilinear structure matches the three ES certificate parameters.
first_step: Write the Type I/II indicator's Fourier expansion, identify the trilinear Kloosterman-fraction sum, and check BC's ranges.
refs: Bettin–Chandee, Trilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions, arXiv:1502.00769

title: Fouvry–Kowalski–Michel trace functions over primes for ES residue indicators
connection: FKM show algebraic trace functions K(n) mod q have Σ_{p≤x} K(p) = o(π(x)) for x ≥ q^{3/4+ε}; ES conditions like '(−p mod 4C) ∈ some set' are trace-function-type functions of p.
why: Gives equidistribution of primes p against arbitrary algebraic weights — e.g. the set of p for which a given finite menu fails mod q.
first_step: Check whether the 'menu failure' indicator mod a prime q (FIXED_MODULUS_SHOTS.md) is a bounded-conductor trace function and apply FKM to get prime densities.
refs: Fouvry–Kowalski–Michel, Algebraic trace functions over the primes, Duke Math. J. 163 (2014)

title: Polymath8 Type III / Deligne estimates for τ3-like ES counts
connection: Polymath8a's Type III estimates use Deligne's RH for correlations of hyper-Kloosterman sums to put τ3 in APs beyond 1/2; ES Type II solution counts are restricted triple-divisor counts (three denominators).
why: τ3-in-APs technology is the natural input for counting ES solutions in APs of n.
first_step: Write f(n) restricted to a fixed residue class of n as a τ3-type sum and test what level of distribution in n the ET average proof needs.
refs: Polymath, New equidistribution estimates of Zhang type, Algebra & Number Theory 8 (2014)

title: Irving / Liu–Shparlinski–Zhang divisor function in APs to smooth or prime-power moduli
connection: Irving (2015) and Liu–Shparlinski–Zhang get τ(n) equidistributed in APs to smooth / prime-power moduli beyond 2/3; ES's tied modulus 4C can be chosen a power of 2 times smooth.
why: Choosing 4C = 2^k is a legitimate ES sub-family (TWO_POWER_LADDER) and prime-power moduli have extra equidistribution.
first_step: Compare TWO_POWER_LADDER.md counts with the divisor-in-AP-to-2^k asymptotic; check which range of k the LSZ theorem covers.
refs: Irving, The divisor function in arithmetic progressions to smooth moduli, IMRN 2015
Liu–Shparlinski–Zhang, Divisor problem in arithmetic progressions modulo a prime power, Adv. Math. (2018)

title: Rosser–Iwaniec semi-linear sieve for 'no divisor ≡ −1 (mod 4C)'
connection: For C = 1, 'N has no divisor ≡ 3 (mod 4)' iff all odd prime factors of N are ≡ 1 (mod 4): a half-dimensional sifted set (Landau–Ramanujan). For general C, ES failure at N requires the prime factors of N to avoid generating −1 in (ℤ/4C)^×.
why: The semi-linear sieve gives sharp upper and lower bounds for such sifted sets; summing over C at fixed p could bound the failure probability.
first_step: For fixed p, compute #{C ≤ X : 4Cp+1 has no divisor ≡ −1 mod 4C} and compare with the semi-linear sieve prediction ∏(1 − 1/ℓ)^{1/2}-type density.
refs: Iwaniec, Rosser's sieve, Acta Arith. 36 (1980)
Friedlander–Iwaniec, Opera de Cribro (2010)

title: Granville–Koukoulopoulos–Matomäki 'when the sieve works'
connection: GKM (Duke 2015) characterise when sifted sets by a set of primes have the expected density; the 'divisors avoid a coset structure' condition in ES is a sifted-set condition on prime factors of 4Cp+1.
why: Precise conditions for sieve heuristics to be correct are what a pointwise lower-tail claim needs.
first_step: Check whether the sifting set 'primes ℓ whose class mod 4C lies in a subgroup H not containing −1' satisfies GKM hypotheses uniformly in C.
refs: Granville–Koukoulopoulos–Matomäki, When the sieve works, Duke Math. J. 164 (2015)

title: Ford–Maynard theory of prime-producing sieves
connection: Ford–Maynard analyse which sieve-theoretic information (Type I/II ranges) can and cannot produce primes, extending the parity problem; ES is a 'one witness among polylog' problem with a parity-like barrier.
why: A formal limit theory for sieve information could make the campaign's B-barriers precise or show a gap.
first_step: Check whether Ford–Maynard's framework (arXiv 2024) includes sequences where the target is 'has a divisor in a class' rather than 'is prime'.
refs: Ford–Maynard, On the theory of prime producing sieves, arXiv:2407.14368

title: Koukoulopoulos–Tao / Ford–Koukoulopoulos–Tao Erdős–Hooley Δ for residue classes
connection: KT and FKT determine the mean of Hooley's Δ(n) = max_u #{d | n : u < d ≤ eu} up to (log log)^{O(1)}; ES needs concentration of divisors of N in a residue class (−1 mod 4C) rather than in a dyadic interval.
why: A 'Δ for residue classes' — max over classes mod m of #{d | N : d ≡ a} — is the ES-native concentration function and its distribution methods (random walks on divisors) may transfer.
first_step: Define Δ_m(N) = max_a #{d|N : d ≡ a mod m} and compute its distribution for N = 4Cp+1 vs random N; read the FKT lower-bound construction.
refs: Koukoulopoulos–Tao, An upper bound on the mean value of the Erdős–Hooley Delta function, arXiv:2306.08615
Ford–Koukoulopoulos–Tao, A lower bound on the mean value of the Erdős–Hooley Delta function, arXiv:2308.11987

title: Ford's divisors-in-intervals H(x,y,2y) method for divisors in residue classes
connection: Ford (Annals 2008) determined the order of #{n ≤ x : n has a divisor in (y,2y]} with a (log)^{−δ}(loglog)^{−3/2} factor; ES needs a divisor in a residue class mod 4C, and the analogous 'has a divisor in class' count.
why: Ford's structure (anatomy, entropy of divisor sets) predicts the shape of the ES lower tail and its failure modes.
first_step: Formulate H_m(x) = #{n ≤ x : n has a divisor ≡ −1 mod m with d ≤ √n} and compute it for m = 4C, C ≤ 50, x = 10^8; compare with Ford-type heuristics.
refs: Ford, The distribution of integers with a divisor in a given interval, Ann. Math. 168 (2008)

title: Deshouillers–Dress–Tenenbaum arcsine law in residue classes
connection: DDT: log d / log n for a random divisor d | n has the arcsine law on average; ES needs divisors d of N in a narrow size window and a residue class.
why: Joint (size, class) distribution of random divisors controls how many ES certificates exist.
first_step: Compute the joint distribution of (log d/log N, d mod 4C) for N = 4Cp+1 and check independence numerically.
refs: Deshouillers–Dress–Tenenbaum, Lois de répartition des diviseurs, Acta Arith. 34 (1979)

title: Erdős primitive-set / Lichtman: ES-covered n as a set of multiples
connection: Since a solution for n gives one for every multiple of n, the set of n covered by any fixed family of identities is a set of multiples ℳ(B) of a primitive set B; Lichtman (2022) proved the Erdős primitive set conjecture Σ 1/(b log b) ≤ Σ_p 1/(p log p).
why: Sets-of-multiples theory (Besicovitch, Erdős, Hall) quantifies how much a family covers and how the uncovered set (divisor-closed) can look.
first_step: For the repo's identity menus up to modulus M, compute the primitive generator set B among primes ≤ 10^7 and the density of ℳ(B); test whether Σ_{b∈B} 1/(b log b) tracks the uncovered density.
refs: Lichtman, A proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture, arXiv:2202.02384
Hall, Sets of Multiples (CUP 1996)

title: Banks–Ford–Tao: probabilistic prime models fail → refine the ES zero law
connection: BFT (Invent. 2023) show Cramér-type random models of primes mispredict large gaps and propose corrected models; the campaign's (J)97 lottery zero law for ES failures is a random model of the same kind.
why: Siblings fail less than the zero law predicts (G4); a BFT-style correction (sieving by small primes first) could explain it.
first_step: Rebuild the ES lottery model with residue-class sieving by primes ≤ z (BFT 'Granville model') and refit to S_{n,−4} and ES_Q1 failure data.
refs: Banks–Ford–Tao, Large prime gaps and probabilistic models, arXiv:1908.08613

title: Harper random multiplicative functions: lower-tail of divisor-character sums
connection: Harper proved better-than-square-root cancellation for low moments of random multiplicative function sums (Forum Pi 2020) via multiplicative chaos; ES counts R(p) are sums over divisors of p-tied integers twisted by characters mod 4C.
why: Multiplicative chaos is the known mechanism for unusual lower tails of divisor-structured sums.
first_step: Model R(p) as Σ_C Σ_{d | 4Cp+1} 1_{d≡−1 (4C)} with prime factorizations randomized, and compute its lower-tail exponent by simulation vs Harper-type predictions.
refs: Harper, Moments of random multiplicative functions, I: low moments, better than squareroot cancellation, and critical multiplicative chaos, arXiv:1703.06654

title: Kozma–Samotij lower tails via relative entropy for R(p)
connection: Kozma–Samotij prove lower-tail large deviations for subgraph counts via relative entropy; R(p) is a count of 'arithmetic subgraphs' (divisor relations) in a random-like structure.
why: ES's core difficulty is the one-sided lower tail R(p) ≥ ε·M_BM(p); entropy methods are the modern lower-tail tool.
first_step: Map the ES certificate count to a polynomial in independent-ish Bernoulli variables (ℓ | 4Cp+1) and check the KS hypotheses (bounded influence) on data.
refs: Kozma–Samotij, Lower tails via relative entropy, arXiv:2104.04850

title: Harel–Mousset–Samotij upper tails via entropic stability (dual for R(p))
connection: HMS 'Upper tails via high moments and entropic stability' gives sharp upper tails for subgraph counts; for ES, upper-tail control of the *failure* indicator counts translates into exceptional-set bounds.
why: Exceptional-set results are upper tails of a 'number of uncovered p' variable.
first_step: Write E(N) as a polynomial count and check whether HMS-type moment methods give anything beyond Vaughan-type bounds.
refs: Harel–Mousset–Samotij, Upper tails via high moments and entropic stability, Duke Math. J. (2022), arXiv:1904.08212

title: Janson/Suen inequality with modern dependency graphs for 'no certificate' event
connection: Janson's inequality bounds P(no event) ≤ exp(−μ + Δ/2) for monotone events; 'no ES certificate at p' is an intersection of complements of divisor events.
why: μ ≍ log²p so exp(−μ) is tiny; the issue is Δ (correlations). Modern refinements (Riordan–Warnke) handle non-monotone dependencies.
first_step: Compute μ and Δ empirically for a hard prime; test Riordan–Warnke's 'Janson inequality for general events' conditions.
refs: Riordan–Warnke, The Janson inequalities for general up-sets, Random Struct. Alg. 46 (2015)

title: Chen–Stein Poisson approximation for the ES certificate count
connection: Stein's method bounds total-variation distance of a count to Poisson; if R(p) were approximately Poisson(μ) with μ ≍ log²p, P(R=0) ≈ e^{−μ}.
why: Gives a quantitative heuristic and identifies which dependencies (shared prime factors) break Poisson behaviour.
first_step: Compute the Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon b1,b2,b3 terms for the ES certificate events at p ≤ 10^6 on data.
refs: Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon, Two moments suffice for Poisson approximations, Ann. Prob. 17 (1989)

title: Granville–Soundararajan pretentiousness of the 'class of divisors' character
connection: Pretentious theory: a multiplicative function f is small on average unless it pretends to be n^{it}χ(n); the indicator of 'N has a divisor in class −1 mod m' expands via characters χ mod m into Σ_χ χ̄(−1) Σ_{d|N} χ(d).
why: The ES failure set is where all such character divisor sums conspire; pretentious distance gives a language for 'conspiracy'.
first_step: For each failing N (no divisor ≡ −1 mod m), compute the pretentious distance D(χ_m-twisted divisor sums) and see whether failures cluster at a pretentious character (e.g. the real character mod m).

title: Koukoulopoulos–Maynard GCD-graph compression (Duffin–Schaeffer)
connection: Koukoulopoulos–Maynard proved Duffin–Schaeffer (Annals 2020) by a compression argument on GCD graphs controlling overlaps between rational approximations a/q; ES is a question about approximating 4/n by short Egyptian sums, with overlap structure between certificates sharing common factors.

connection: Petrow–Young (Annals 2020) prove the Weyl-strength subconvex bound L(1/2,χ) ≪ q^{1/6+ε} for all Dirichlet χ; ES counts expand over characters mod 4C.

connection: Kelley–Meka get quasi-polynomial bounds for 3-AP-free sets via almost-periodicity + spectral positivity; the ES e-slice asks whether −1 lies in the quotient set Q = {ab⁻¹ : ab | N} ⊂ (ℤ/e)^×, an additive-combinatorial (multiplicative-group) statement.

title: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa (Gowers–Green–Manners–Tao) for divisor quotient sets
connection: PFR (Marton) over 𝔽₂ⁿ and torsion-free groups: small doubling ⇒ covered by few cosets of a subgroup; the set of prime factors of N mod e generates the ES quotient set.

title: Balandraud's sharp subset-sum theorem in ℤ/p for the 'target −1' problem
connection: Balandraud: subset sums of k distinct nonzero residues mod a prime cover ≥ min(p, k(k+1)/2+1) elements; taking discrete logs, ES's subset-products of prime factors of N in (ℤ/e)^× is a subset-sum problem in ℤ/(e−1).

connection: For prime e, −1 ∈ H ⊂ 𝔽_e^× iff |H| is even; the e-slice needs −1 in the quotient set Q (not the generated subgroup), but −1 ∈ ⟨Q⟩ is a necessary condition expressed via 2-adic valuations of multiplicative orders.

refs: Moree, Artin's primitive root conjecture – a survey, arXiv:math/0412262

connection: Bourgain's sum-product and exponential-sum bounds for arbitrary q handle composite moduli; ES moduli 4C, 4cd are composite and smooth.

connection: Huang's proof uses a signed adjacency matrix of the hypercube and Cauchy interlacing to force a high-degree vertex in any large induced subgraph; ES certificates live on a product of small 'choice' cubes (choice of prime factors into a,b).
